title: ActionCable hook can replay stale data after channel changes
reasoning: useActionCable keeps its data state across channelName/identifier changes and does not clear it when a new subscription is created. A component that switches from one session channel to another can briefly expose the previous channel's last part/status payload. useSessionParts includes sessionId in the consuming effect dependencies, so a sessionId change can cause the old payload to be processed for the new session, scrolling to an unrelated part or invalidating the new session's queries before any event is received on the new channel.
recommendation: Reset data to null when the identifier or subscribed events change, ideally before creating the new subscription, or include channel identity with received payloads and ignore payloads not belonging to the active channel.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: useActionCable tests mount a single channel and emit events, but do not rerender with a different channel after data has been received. useSessionParts tests also do not cover changing sessionId after a live part/status update.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a useActionCable rerender test that emits data on channel_1, rerenders with channel_2, and asserts result.current is null until a channel_2 event arrives. Add a useSessionParts sessionId-change test if stale scroll behavior is important.
minimumFixScope: app/hooks/useActionCable.ts state lifecycle and a focused hook rerender test
